title: Спор с Михаилом продолжается  (The Bet with Mikhail Continues)

segments.t: Defeated by the massive slab of meat on his plate, Mikhail concedes the first round to Barinov—but warns that the promotion ends the moment he brings a man who can eat the entire entrecôte.
Ну так что, я ввожу акцию?
Но если я приведу человека, который съест твой антрекот.
Смотри, она у тебя за спиной стоит.
Now let's go back through their conversation line by line and unpack the Russian phrasing.
'My youngest daughter would eat more than that.' In Russian, the idea of 'my' flows naturally into 'will eat' without extra filler words.
Ну так что, я ввожу акцию?
'Well then, am I introducing the promotion?' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'come on' and finishing on 'promotion'. Mikhail answers right away.
'Introduce it, introduce it.' Notice how Russian expresses 'introduce' and 'introduce' with crisp inflection rather than helper words.
Но если я приведу человека, который съест твой антрекот.
'But if I bring a person who eats your entrecote.' The grammar packs 'but' and 'entrecote' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange.
'The promotion ends, got it?' Mikhail raises the pitch on 'understood' to turn the phrase into a direct spoken question. Chef Barinov answers right away.
'Mishanya, you are a masochist.' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'Mishanya' before landing on 'masochist'.
'You love losing, huh?' The meaning hinges on 'love' working together with 'yes' in spoken Russian.
'Well, has your hysterical wife calmed down?' Senya raises the pitch on 'calmed down' to turn the phrase into a direct spoken question. Chef Barinov answers right away.
'Who is hysterical?' Chef Barinov brings out the contrast between 'who' and 'hysterical woman' in a few short words.
'I am talking about my wife.' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'I' and finishing on 'speak'.
Смотри, она у тебя за спиной стоит.
'Look, she is standing right behind you.' Chef Barinov brings out the contrast between 'watch' and 'she' in a few short words. Senya answers right away.
'Oh, anything but that!' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'oh' before landing on 'this'. Alright, let's hear the entire conversation one more time from start to finish.
Ну так что, я ввожу акцию?
Но если я приведу человека, который съест твой антрекот.
Смотри, она у тебя за спиной стоит.
Senya turns around in horror to find Marina standing right in the kitchen wearing a hotel uniform. See you next time!
